daily.title: UN approves world map reflecting true size of Africa
daily.summary: The UN General Assembly voted to adopt a map that more accurately shows the size of the continents. Only the United States voted against the measure, which projects the country as smaller than on traditional maps.

daily.title: Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
daily.summary: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

daily.title: Yemen: Fighting intensifies amid Houthi push in the west
daily.summary: Houthi forces are trying to secure high ground and solidify their control of the entry to the Red Sea in the southwest. The Iran-backed militia abandoned a shaky truce with the Saudi-backed government-in-exile in July.

daily.title: Saxony-Anhalt: Small parties will be the kingmakers
daily.summary: The far-right AfD has good odds of winning an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's parliament this state election, enabling them to govern alone. It all depends on whether other parties make the cut.

daily.title: Germany's alliance against the far right
daily.summary: Trade unions, churches and human rights activists are worried about the rise of the far-right AfD. How can civil society protect people who are threatened by far-right extremism?

daily.title: Nigeria: Suspected oil thieves dead after inhaling fumes
daily.summary: A Nigerian environmental group says that at least 37 people died trying to siphon crude oil off a ship illegally. Police acknowledged a fatal incident but gave fewer details, saying investigations continued.

daily.title: Germany, partners aim to finalize 'return hubs' by year end
daily.summary: German Interior Minister Dobrindt said "technical discussions" were underway with non-EU countries to establish controversial "return hubs." Rights organizations have questioned the legality and morality of the plans.

daily.title: Nepal flood disaster puts climate justice under spotlight
daily.summary: The devastating Himalayan glacial floods have raised broader questions about who should bear the costs and responsibility for the impacts of climate-related disasters.

daily.title: How can African retailers compete with Shein and Temu?
daily.summary: Shein and Temu are expanding across Africa with low prices and vast product ranges. Businesses and unions warn the growth could come at a cost for local jobs.

daily.title: How vulnerable is Germany's infrastructure?
daily.summary: The growing number of attacks on substations and railway lines in Germany is raising concern. Experts say that people will have to get used to the likelihood that such incidents will continue.

daily.title: Romania prosecutors indict Andrew Tate for trafficking minors
daily.summary: The social media influencer has also been indicted for money laundering and sex with a minor. His brother Tristan has been indicted for complicity.

daily.title: Majority of Germans see Russia as a threat
daily.summary: More than half of German citizens believe that Germany's security is threatened by Russia, according to the latest survey by public broadcaster ARD.

daily.title: Two Reform UK officials resign amid donation breach reports
daily.summary: A Channel 4 report alleges that the party officials accepted foreign donations to fund three polls, illegal under the UK's electoral law. The allegations, which the party denies, come amid its annual conference.

daily.title: Germany news: Police raid vehicle of suspected grid saboteur
daily.summary: A suspicious object that could damage power lines has been found near a German substation for a third time this week. Meanwhile, Germany and EU partners are aiming to finalize 'return hubs' by year end.

daily.title: The hidden environmental cost of AI data centers
daily.summary: As data centers multiply to meet AI demand, they're straining power grids, draining water supplies and reshaping the land and air around them.

daily.title: Serbia: How the funeral of Ratko Mladic is dividing a nation
daily.summary: As the Serbian government leaves the decision about Ratko Mladic's funeral arrangements to his family, international pressure on the country is mounting. How do Serbs feel about the matter?

daily.title: Germany: Is Saxony-Anhalt's economy really struggling?
daily.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party has long claimed that the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt has been left behind. Is that really the case? A closer look at the data offers some interesting insights.

daily.title: Why the North Korean women's football team is so good
daily.summary: North Korea's young footballers enter the U-20 World Cup in Poland as defending champions — the 2024 title was their third. Why is the isolated state so good at the game?

daily.title: India news: ISRO launces first imaging satellite into orbit
daily.summary: The newly launched satellite will hover some 36,000 kilometers above Earth and is being called India's "eye in the sky." DW has the latest.

daily.title: 2026 Beethoven Festival evokes a sense of home
daily.summary: The motto of this year's classical music festival in Bonn is "Home/At Home," featuring musicians from diverse cultures presenting pieces from their homelands.

daily.title: How Volkswagen's huge workforce became a costly burden
daily.summary: The struggling German carmaker plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs from its 630,000-strong workforce. How did VW's headcount get so bloated, and will the cuts be enough to survive the Chinese EV onslaught?

weekly.title: Berlin: BER Airport Terminal 1 reopened after security scare
weekly.summary: Police have given the all-clear at Terminal 1 at Berlin's BER Airport following an earlier security scare and evacuation. The airport said some flights had been delayed but they were trying to avoid any cancelations.

weekly.title: Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
weekly.summary: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to pay Naftogaz damages.

weekly.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination
weekly.summary: Migration is a sensitive topic in Germany, with public debate dominated by the fear of uncontrolled immigration. People forget that, over two centuries, millions of Germans emigrated in search of a better life.

weekly.title: Is Germany's economic slump finally over?
weekly.summary: Despite a slew of negative headlines, the German economy has posted its best figures in years. There are reasons for optimism, but structural issues remain.

weekly.title: Germany news: Police say arson attack targeted defense firm
weekly.summary: Two people were arrested in connection with a small fire at a construction site near a defense tech company in Munich. Investigators are looking at a possible "political motive."

weekly.title: Russia to close branches of Germany's Goethe-Institut
weekly.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the move was in response to Germany's decision to close the Russian House in Berlin after blaming Moscow for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

weekly.title: Germany: How to woo voters with an immigrant background
weekly.summary: The number of voters in Germany with an immigrant background is rising. Yet the established parties barely manage to reach them. Why not?

weekly.title: Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
weekly.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with the UK monarch and relatively new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

weekly.title: Russia's hybrid attacks on Germany: how should Berlin react?
weekly.summary: Germany holds Russia responsible for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport. But critics say Berlin's response, including the closure of Russia's consulate in Bonn, has been too timid.

weekly.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations
weekly.summary: Austria are getting ready for their first Women's Ice Hockey World Championship. But preparations have been overshadowed by a dispute about conditions, pay and getting men's cast-off kit. A solution now looks in sight.

weekly.title: EU summons Russian envoy over failed Leipzig drone attack
weekly.summary: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the attempted attack had "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism." She said the EU was summoning a Russian envoy, with France announcing a similar step.

weekly.title: Women's football: Anyomi, London City and the German exodus
weekly.summary: Nicole Anyomi has joined Alexia Putellas and other star names in signing for the ambitious English club London City Lionesses. The Germany winger told DW England is a better place to develop her game than back home.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Russia threatens 'devastating' Baltic response
weekly.summary: Any escalation in the Baltic region will lead to a significant response, Moscow said.

weekly.title: Germany says Russia behind attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
weekly.summary: Investigators believe an explosives-laden drone was deliberately targeting a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport in early August. The German government said on Tuesday that it held Russia "responsible."

weekly.title: Germany terminates lease for Berlin's Russian House
weekly.summary: Germany has announced the termination of the lease for the Russian House in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it is a hub for propaganda and espionage.

weekly.title: Can communities be proteced from melting glaciers?
weekly.summary: Rising temperatures are increasing the risk of floods and avalanches in mountain regions. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet shows the urgent need for solutions, and the tools that could help save lives.

weekly.title: Mladic's death, Bosnia and Serbia's unfinished reckoning
weekly.summary: The death of Ratko Mladic did not close a dark chapter of European history; it reopened old wounds. The ideology that created him lives on. The Dayton peace agreement ended the war, not the divisions that produced it.

weekly.title: Norway's new King Haakon VIII takes oath in parliament
weekly.summary: The new king swore to uphold the constitution in parliament in Oslo, the first major institutional step of his reign. Haakon VIII's wife Queen Mette-Marit had to skip the event in the aftermath of her lung transplant.

weekly.title: Germany's center-left SPD is fighting for survival
weekly.summary: The Social Democratic Party is sinking ever deeper into crisis. Voters are turning away, while unrest is growing within its grassroots ranks. Will upcoming state elections accelerate the party's downward spiral?

weekly.title: US irks Germany, Europe with Russian G20 invite, press bans
weekly.summary: Russia's finance minister is at the G20 meeting in Asheville but some key US press corps members are not. The mood was already tense amid the lengthy Iran war and Trump's renewed beef with neighbor Canada.

weekly.title: Can new Apple CEO John Ternus fix the tech giant's AI woes?
weekly.summary: John Ternus is just the third Apple CEO in 30 years. His primary challenge is to correct the company's faltering AI strategy to preserve its position as a big tech leader.

weekly.title: Ulrich Siegmund wants to make Saxony-Anhalt a model for AfD rule
weekly.summary: The AfD's lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund aims to turn his small federal state into a blueprint for right-wing extremist politics across Germany.

weekly.title: At Venice Film Festival, politics take center stage
weekly.summary: With works about Gaza, Ukraine and Elon Musk, political cinema is in the spotlight at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

weekly.title: Canada's Carney holds firm against Trump tariffs
weekly.summary: Canada is facing new US import penalties after Prime Minister Mark Carney refused to match US tariffs on China. Other countries are watching as the Trump trade clash turns into a fight over economic sovereignty.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt State Premier Schulze takes on far-right AfD
weekly.summary: The AfD is far ahead in the polls in Saxony-Anhalt. But Schulze is determined to keep the AfD from becoming the first far-right party since World War II to lead a German state government.

weekly.title: Inside the sea cucumber smuggling boom
weekly.summary: A quiet multimillion‑dollar black market is exploding across the Indian Ocean, driven by one unlikely animal: the sea cucumber.

weekly.title: Ailing Djokovic 'despised' every moment of US Open defeat
weekly.summary: Novak Djokovic has exited in the first round of a Grand Slam for the first time in over two decades. Could time — or an unknown health condition — be catching up with the Serbian tennis legend?

weekly.title: Germany news: Summer was 2nd hottest of the century — DWD
weekly.summary: Germany's DWD weather service says the summer was second only to 2003 in terms of average temperatures. It was also unusually dry. In Cologne, police are seeking a man who fired shots at a cafe storefront.

weekly.title: Fact check: Germany's Merz misstates record in ARD interview
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz made several misleading claims on migration, debt and electric vehicles in his summer interview with German public broadcaster ARD.

weekly.title: German churches speak out against AfD ahead of state election
weekly.summary: As the far-right AfD party leads the polls ahead of Sunday's election in Saxony-Anhalt, church leaders have warned against downplaying its "ethnonationalist" agenda.

weekly.title: EU wants drones to spray pesticides, but it could backfire
weekly.summary: The EU wants to lift a decades-old ban on spraying pesticides from the air, allowing drones to be used for greater precision. But experts warn the plan could lead to even more pesticides being used in agriculture.

weekly.title: Greece, Turkey clash over protected Aegean marine areas
weekly.summary: Turkey has announced the creation of two protected zones in a disputed area of the Aegean Sea, sparking an angry reaction from Greece. Does this mark a new chapter in a long-running dispute between the two countries?

weekly.title: Russian-American heads Trump's planned Caucasus trade route
weekly.summary: A Russian-born businessman heads the investment fund financing the so-called "Trump Route," a planned corridor through Armenia linking Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan. Who is Konstantin Sokolov, and what role does he play?

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt election: Why the AfD is so strong
weekly.summary: The AfD is polling above 40% ahead of Saxony-Anhalt's election on September 6. What is driving support for the far right in this predominantly rural eastern German state?

weekly.title: This extremely successful author polarizes German readers
weekly.summary: She's young and she says what she thinks: Caroline Wahl is topping Germany's bestseller lists with her novels. But she has also faced a public backlash.

weekly.title: Serbia keeps EU, Russia in play ahead of key election
weekly.summary: As Serbia heads toward an uncertain election, President Aleksandar Vucic is balancing ties with Russia and EU ambitions. But growing geopolitical tensions and pressure at home are narrowing his room to maneuver.
